content_html_sanitized:
Posted November 21, 2003
Special Report to MarijuanaNews readers by Richard Cowan

At the beginning of 2003 it seemed likely that Canada was well on its way to an imperfect but sincere effort to ameliorate the problems caused by cannabis prohibition, beginning with some form of decriminalization.

However, after the Justice Minister took the extraordinary step of submitting a draft of the bill to Washington for its approval even before he consulted his own party caucus, the process has rapidly deteriorated.
See
Canada's New Decriminalization Bill To Be Delayed After Justice Minister's Trip to Washington, and Health Minister's Trip to the Marvelous World Of Marijuana Make-Believe. John Walters In Drag?

As the time remaining before Prime Minister Chretien's retirement grew shorter and shorter, a false sense of urgency was used to justify a rush to pass any bill that would be approved by the police and the most prohibitionist elements in the Parliament.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.

Saved by the bell?

Fortunately, this gadarene rush was interrupted by the politics of the Liberal party, and the Parliament has now been adjourned for about two months. If, as expected, the bill is revived under the new Prime Minister, Paul Martin, a prohibitionist, the push to make it worse will also be revived.
See
The Next Prime Minister of Canada Talks War On Us. Looming Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Proves Need for International Debate On Cannabis Prohibition.

Consequently, the Canadian cannabis communities must use this reprieve to organize an effective national response, and I intend to devote all of my efforts for the next two months to providing them with a steady stream of reports and commentary on MarijuanaNews and on special programs on Pot-TV, that I am calling the Battle for Canada.

Today I recorded the first program of the series.

We need to provide our allies in the media and the Parliament with the maximum possible support. We have the facts. We have the arguments. But we do not have the momentum or the ears of the members of Parliament. That must change, quickly. Also, I will be calling for unity in the cannabis communities to meet the urgent challenge ahead.

In addition to informing Parliament and the media about cannabis, we must also make clear to them that they have been lied to by the Canadian police and by the US government.
See
The Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Escalates. Blatant Drive to Create DEAland Style Police State. Phony Decrim Bill Gets Even Worse.

I have a vast amount of material on MarijuanaNews that I want to reorganize and use to educate the Canadian media and politicians. I will also be more persistent in calling for an international debate on cannabis prohibition, a something that I have urged from time to time.
See
We Live In Interesting Times: Chaos in Cannabis Prohibition Around the World. Does John Walters Really Want A National Debate on Marijuana Prohibition?

Check out today's program and let me know what you think.

I was a little out of practice, but I'll bet (as Bill Bennett would say) that I wasn't as nervous as Rush Limbaugh was on his first day back.

For several months my attention has been focused on helping my friends, the Kubbys, Steve Tuck and Ken Hayes, with their refugee claims, but now that process has come to an end.
See
If Cannabis Could Cure Cancer, They Would Tell Us, Right? No. Very Simply, It Would Undermine Cannabis Prohibition. Steve Kubby Is The Living Proof.
and
Placer County: Still Crazy After All These Years. Kubby Hearings Offer New Evidence California Law Enforcement Still Fighting Medical Cannabis Law. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com
and
Tuck Refugee Hearings End. The Facts Put Canada In Awkward Position. Catching A Nark In A Lie? Imagine That! News and Analysis by Richard Cowan.

The Kubbys have been notified that that Canada's Immigration and Refugee Board has made a final decision on whether American medical marijuana advocates Steve and Michele Kubby are entitled to permanent refugee status in Canada. The 60-page decision was officially entered on Tuesday November 18th, but must await translation into French before it is released

It is not certain when it will be made public, but we are expecting it to be next week. Whenever it happens I will have a special report on MarijuanaNews and the following day, there will be a press conference on Pot-TV. I am optimistic, but the Canadian government is expected to appeal, if we win. (The decisions on Tuck and Hayes will probably be announced by the end of the year.) It will be years before the process is completed, but at least our friends will be safe from the predators in the meantime.

(Starting next week, MarijuanaNews updates will be posted on Wednesdays.)
